newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real rises 0.02 pct on small mini-band move - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real rises 0.02 pct on small mini-band move - Sept 24.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.02 percent to close at 1.0195 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank surprised traders by lowering the mini-band only 0.05 percent, dealers said.
The Central Bank set the new real-dollar mini-band between 1.0195 and 1.0245 per dollar through a buy/sell auction before the open.
The market was surprised as it had expected a drop of 0.1 percent in the mini-band, the rate at which the Central Bank has lowered it in recent depreciations, dealers added.
The previous mini-band was set on September 17 between 1.019 and 1.024 to the dollar.
The Central Bank's move also reinforced expectations of a smaller drop in the mini-band for the month of September.
In recent months, the Central Bank has been lowering the mini-band 0.6 percent a month. So far this month, it has lowered the mini-band by 0.34 percent.
"Nobody is sure, but since the Central Bank lowered the band just 0.05 percent today, there is a good chance this month the mini-band will end up with a 0.6 percent drop," one trader said.
The real also rose today due to dollar inflows, dealers said. Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Tuesday surplus of $85 million.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real fell 0.03 percent to end at 1.0252 real per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed steady at 1.038 real per greenback, traders said.
